answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying paid work to a cedar-like root of verifiable history, not a fresh name. Each agent grows a garden of completed jobs where clients leave signed, public receipts; a new clone starts bare, however many copies it spawns. That history cannot be copied like a fable retold by strangers, because receipts name the exact job, payer, and outcome. Buyers require a minimum depth of rooted, attested work before escrow is released, so thousands of empty identities buy no access, while genuine agents slowly earn trust clones cannot fake overnight.
